## Triage: p2 · `domain:ui` · `pm:queue` · 2026-11-02T06:35Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- Read fresh. The mobile shell (objectstack-ai/mobile 2.0) hosts the web Console and injects `window.ObjectStackNative`. This card makes the Console detect it (`useNativeHost()` in `ui/packages/mobile`) and adapt its chrome. The work is entirely in `ui/**`, so it is `domain:ui`: the mobile project's cards in this repo go to the existing lanes. The bridge contract is owned by the mobile repo (`docs/HYBRID-SHELL.md`), and nothing here adds an ObjectStack protocol key, so p2. #29042 is blocked on it.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Scope addition from the mobile side (objectstack-ai/mobile#144, patch round in progress):

When the shell opens a Console route (a notification tap, an app link, or a bridge `navigate` call), it no longer reloads the page. It dispatches a cancelable `objectstack-native:navigate` event on `window`, with `detail.route` set to a Console route that the shell has already checked against path escape. It falls back to a full `location.assign` only when no listener calls `preventDefault()`.

The shell-mode work in this card should therefore also:

- listen for `objectstack-native:navigate`;
- navigate with the Console's own router to `detail.route`;
- call `preventDefault()`, so the Console bundle is not reloaded on every notification tap.

Acceptance addition: dispatching the event in shell mode moves the router without a document reload, and outside shell mode the listener is not installed.

**For the maintainer · safe-area padding · 2026-11-02T08:13Z.** ⛔ Not a claim. @hotlong, PR #29140 does not take one line of the Ask, and this records why.

- **Ask 2** says the Console "pads with the `--os-native-safe-*` variables", following `docs/HYBRID-SHELL.md` in objectstack-ai/mobile.
- **Measured:** the os-dev read objectstack-ai/mobile#144 at `443207c`. `components/shell/ConsoleWebView.tsx` wraps the WebView in a `View` with `paddingTop: insets.top` and `paddingBottom: insets.bottom`, unconditionally.
- **Seat's ruling:** if the Console also padded, the top and bottom insets would double. So the shell stays the single owner of the safe area, and the Console pads nothing in shell mode. The variables stay readable for any later surface that opts in.
- **For the mobile side:** either `HYBRID-SHELL.md` drops the line about the Console padding with the variables, or the shell stops padding its WebView and the Console takes it over. Seat 4 cannot change the mobile repository. If you want the Console to own the padding, say so here and a follow-up card does it.

Acceptance addition: keep shell mode platform-neutral.

The mobile shell is the first host of `window.ObjectStackNative`, but not necessarily the last. A desktop shell (Tauri, same bridge) is the recorded future shape if a desktop need ever appears. To keep that free for the Console:

- Never infer "phone" from the presence of the bridge. Read `ObjectStackNative.platform` for the host, and use the viewport and breakpoints, not the host, for layout decisions.
- Gate every native call on `ObjectStackNative.has(capability)`, never on platform name.
- Treat `platform` as an open set on the Console side (today `ios` / `android`; `desktop` may follow), with no exhaustive switch that breaks on a new value.

Acceptance addition: a fake bridge reporting an unknown `platform` with a subset of capabilities renders shell mode without errors, and only the announced capabilities are used.
